foundation.frost_design: Engineered pile depth and uplift resistance below frost; geotechnical review required.

name: Woodland Cottage
tagline: A compact, step-free cottage under a pitched roof, with a covered porch and direct garden access.
description: A single-storey 40-foot container cottage with an accessible internal route and washroom. The plan is deliberately simple: bedroom, bathroom, entrance hall, kitchen and living. The 2.8 m bathroom contains a modeled 1.5 m turning circle; the shared-path grades and professional accessibility review remain outstanding.

architecture.intent: Single-storey baseline with a pitched roof and a covered garden porch.

roof_form.drainage: Gable roof drains to two eaves; gutters, downpipes and splash protection need detailing.
roof_form.snow: Snow slides from a 24° roof; snow guards and entry protection need review.
roof_form.wind: Gable ends and overhangs need wind-uplift review.
roof_form.maintenance: Roof and gutter access needs a safe plan.
roof_form.note: Roof geometry is conceptual and independent of the container geometry. It does not create an occupied storey.

structure.notes: Single-storey module; openings still need framing review.

zones.name: Sleeping
zones.accessibility: Ground-floor bedroom; verify a 1.5 m turning circle and a 0.9 m route.

zones.name: Bathroom
zones.accessibility: Adaptable bathroom intent; verify transfer space, grab-bar blocking and door clearance.

zones.name: Kitchen
zones.accessibility: Provide a lowered work section and clear approach.

solar.mounting: fixed tilt, due south; snow-shedding; roof structure and wind uplift need review
solar.source: SolarCalculator.CA Ottawa: 39° optimal fixed tilt; brief range 36–39° year-round, winter ~60°, summer ~30°, due south.
solar.note: True south; confirm magnetic declination, shading, snow shedding and structural fixing.

access.path_connection: Step-free route to the shared path is a design intent; the connection and grades are not surveyed.
access.vertical_access_strategy: Single occupied storey; no internal stair.
access.standards: Project targets informed by the Ontario Building Code and CSA B651. No code compliance, licence or professional accessibility review is claimed.

features.solar: South roof slope is solar-ready; no production is calculated.
features.green_roof: Green roof not included unless explicitly recorded.
features.environment: Small footprint, external insulation and a replaceable rainscreen; no carbon or energy result is claimed.
features.outdoor: 5.4 × 2.8 m covered porch and a level garden deck
features.accessibility: Ground-floor living with a step-free entrance and an adaptable bathroom target. Not a compliance assessment.

thermal.wall_insulation_strategy: continuous external insulation with thermal breaks at openings, pile caps and service penetrations
thermal.thermal_bridge_mitigation: continuous external insulation and thermal breaks at openings and pile caps
thermal.air_vapour_control: exterior-insulated, vapour-open assembly; sealed interior air barrier (to be detailed)
thermal.window_performance: triple glazed, low-e, argon, thermally broken frames
thermal.notes: Conceptual thermal intent only. No energy or code calculation.

envelope.thermal_breaks: continuous external insulation with thermal washers and stainless fasteners; breaks at openings, pile caps and service penetrations
envelope.air_vapour_control: exterior-insulated, vapour-open assembly with a sealed interior air barrier; joints and service penetrations to be detailed
envelope.fire: combustible insulation, cladding and cavity need a fire review; cavity barriers, cladding classification and separation are not resolved
envelope.fastening: long fasteners pass through the insulation into the steel frame; pull-out, corrosion, thermal bridging and water shedding need engineering review
envelope.penetrations: openings, cladding rails, planter brackets and service penetrations need structural and waterproofing review
envelope.maintenance: inspect cladding, sealant, cavity, fasteners and vegetation twice a year and after severe weather
envelope.notes: Conceptual assembly only. Not code-compliant or moisture-safe until reviewed by a building-envelope engineer.

fire.note: Fire measures are design intentions, not a fire-resistance rating, WUI approval or insurance guarantee.

entry_shelter.note: Reused container-door leaves can form a shelter and shutters; hinges, wind uplift, egress, fire and security need review.

accessibility.notes: 2.8 m bathroom with a modeled 1.5 m turning circle. Fixtures and transfers still require professional review.

circulation.note: Concept 1.2 m route; thresholds and crossfall are not surveyed.

service.note: Water heater and electrical service reserve; not sized.

provenance.method: Authored accessible concept interior for Phase 3.
provenance.verification: None. Conceptual; not a professional accessibility assessment.

water.note: Conceptual system intent. No tank size, location, yield, freeze protection, treatment or fire-service connection is designed. A rain barrel is not a system and is not a fire reserve.

reference_module.label: 450 W reference module
reference_module.source: Illustrative 450 W module, about 1.76 x 1.13 m. Confirm the chosen module datasheet and dimensions.

occupancy.label: Seasonal summer use with intermittent winter visits
limitations: Designed for seasonal use; the water system is winterized when the cottage is empty.
A three-to-five-day winter cloud sequence needs a plan, not just a larger battery.
Roof area, not demand, is the practical limit on this array.
occupancy.notes: The cottage is intended for summer and shoulder-season use, with weekend or short winter visits. It is not presented as a full-time winter home, although the modelled electricity balance is relatively favourable because the demand is small.

maintenance.note: One flush row at the south eave; access from a stable ladder and a roof anchor. A roofer or solar installer should service it.

snow.note: Snow guards and a 1.2 m gravel strip keep sliding snow off the garden doors. Confirm with the roof and eave design.

shading.note: Woodland edge and the porch roof shade the lower array in winter mornings and afternoons.

losses.note: Losses are applied once each. Battery charge and discharge losses are applied in the battery simulation, not here.

solar.note: Simplified geometric shading from the fictional woodland scatter. Not a measured shade study.

loads.name: Refrigerator, 45–60 L DC compressor
loads.seasonal_variation: Higher duty in summer; lower in winter when the cabin is cool.
loads.source: Manufacturer-typical 12/24 V compressor fridge; 35% duty at about 20 °C.
loads.notes: Food storage is a minimum load even for a small home. Confirm the chosen unit and its duty cycle.

loads.name: Interior LED lighting
loads.seasonal_variation: Winter evenings need more lighting than summer.
loads.source: Six to ten 5–9 W LED fixtures, used for the stated hours.
loads.notes: Assume DC LED luminaires on a 24 V or 48 V bus with local switching.

loads.name: Exterior LED lighting and entry light
loads.seasonal_variation: Long winter nights and short summer nights.
loads.source: One 12 W entry and path luminaire with timer or manual control.
loads.notes: Dark-sky friendly, shielded and timed; no continuous floodlighting.

loads.name: USB-C charging
loads.seasonal_variation: More charging when more people are present.
loads.source: Two 25 W USB-C ports at partial load, two to three hours.
loads.notes: DC-native; avoids running the inverter for small devices.

loads.name: Phones and tablets
loads.source: Two devices at about 15 W average charging power.
loads.notes: Resident devices; not a site load.

loads.name: Laptop computer
loads.seasonal_variation: More remote work in winter; less outdoors in summer.
loads.source: One 45 W laptop with mixed charging and use.
loads.notes: Quantity changes with household size in the explorer.

loads.name: Internet router and local network
loads.source: 10 W router or LTE gateway running continuously.
loads.notes: Kept on for monitoring and remote communication even when unoccupied.

loads.name: LTE or fixed-wireless radio
loads.source: 5 W radio modem running continuously.
loads.notes: No fibre is assumed in the woodland.

loads.name: HRV or ERV ventilation
loads.seasonal_variation: Higher duty in winter because windows stay closed.
loads.source: 28 W ECM fan at low speed; 35–50% effective duty with boost periods.
loads.notes: Required for a tight envelope. Confirm airflow, frost protection and controls.

loads.name: Ceiling fans
loads.source: One 25 W DC ceiling fan.
loads.notes: Reduces the need for active cooling.

loads.name: Water pressure pump
loads.seasonal_variation: Slightly more use when more people are present.
loads.source: 400 W booster pump, about 7–10 minutes per day.
loads.notes: Rainwater or shallow-well supply with a pressure tank.

loads.name: Sensors, controllers and freeze monitoring
loads.source: Sensor node, controller and low-power display.
loads.notes: Supports freeze protection and remote monitoring.

loads.name: Battery management system
loads.source: BMS and shunts, 3 W.
loads.notes: Included in the battery system, not the inverter.

loads.name: Inverter standby
loads.source: 7 W standby when the inverter is on; 3 W in eco mode when unoccupied.
loads.notes: Keep the inverter off at night or when the cabin is empty where the design allows.

loads.name: Induction cooking
loads.source: One portable 1,800 W induction burner at 75% average power while cooking.
loads.notes: Deferrable within the day; a shared kitchen can absorb larger events.

loads.name: Electric kettle
loads.source: 1,200 W kettle, one to three short boils per day.
loads.notes: High instantaneous load; check inverter surge.

loads.name: Toaster or small grill
loads.source: 800 W appliance used briefly.
loads.notes: Ordinary small appliance.

loads.name: Blender or hand mixer
loads.source: 300 W appliance used for a few minutes.
loads.notes: Small kitchen appliance.

loads.name: Battery enclosure heating
loads.seasonal_variation: Winter only; LiFePO4 charging below 0 °C is not allowed.
loads.source: Thermostatically controlled 35 W pad; average duty about 18% in winter.
loads.notes: The enclosure is insulated and kept above freezing. Confirm the heater control and failure mode.

loads.name: Water treatment (UV and filtration)
loads.seasonal_variation: More treatment when demand is higher.
loads.source: UV lamp and controller rated 20 W, two to three hours per day.
loads.notes: Required only if the water source needs treatment; confirm with water testing.

profiles.label: Summer occupation
profiles.notes: Long days, high solar availability, low lighting demand. Discretionary loads can run when the battery is full.

profiles.label: Spring and autumn occupation
profiles.notes: More lighting, variable ventilation and more cloudy periods.

profiles.label: Intermittent winter occupation
profiles.notes: Weekend or short visits. Essential loads run continuously; discretionary loads are reduced. The home is unoccupied between visits.

profiles.label: Unoccupied winter
profiles.notes: Monitoring, battery management, low-power sensors, communications and battery heating only.

battery.location: Insulated service bay beside the kitchen, above floor level.
battery.note: 24 V is retained for a small cabin to keep the battery and inverter range modest. Confirm the inverter surge for the induction burner and kettle.

optional_profiles.label: Cold-climate air-source heat pump
optional_profiles.note: Heating is excluded from the base residential estimates. A heat pump would roughly double or triple winter electricity demand and requires a much larger array and battery, or shared heating.

optional_profiles.label: Conventional electric domestic hot water
optional_profiles.note: Not included in the base. A heat-pump water heater would use roughly one third of this.

optional_profiles.label: Heat-pump water heater
optional_profiles.note: Lower demand than resistance hot water, but it needs a heated, ventilated location and adds compressor noise.

optional_profiles.label: Electric laundry (washer and dryer)
optional_profiles.note: A vented or heat-pump dryer is a large flexible load. The shared lodge is the preferred location.

optional_profiles.label: Additional electric cooking appliances
optional_profiles.note: A second oven or a large induction range increases both daily energy and peak demand.

optional_profiles.label: Electric vehicle charging
optional_profiles.note: Even modest commuting would dominate the residential array. Shared charging at the lodge, with a separate solar canopy, is the sensible location.

options.label: Independent residence
options.description: Each residence relies on its own array and battery.
options.note: No shared electricity is assumed. A five-day winter cloud event must be met by load reduction, an emergency generator or accepting a shortfall.

options.label: Independent with community backup
options.description: The residence keeps essential independent capability but can draw limited supplementary electricity from the common lodge.
options.note: The connection is sized for essential and limited ordinary loads, not for electric heating. It is not guaranteed during a region-wide outage.

options.label: Shared community microgrid
options.description: Multiple arrays and batteries contribute to a professionally designed shared electrical network.
options.note: A microgrid shares supply and demand but does not remove the effect of region-wide winter cloud, snow or a failed shared inverter.

shared.governance_note: Shared infrastructure needs a written governance and cost-allocation agreement that preserves resident autonomy and equitable access.
shared.note: Shared electricity is modeled as an option. The independent case remains the default for each residence.

scenarios.label: Typical summer day
scenarios.note: Synthetic clear summer day. Not a weather forecast.

scenarios.label: Typical winter day
scenarios.note: Synthetic average winter day. Not a weather forecast.

scenarios.label: Five consecutive cloudy winter days
scenarios.note: Synthetic overcast sequence. The battery is not allowed to fall below its reserve in ordinary operation.

scenarios.label: Snow-covered solar panels
scenarios.note: Zero generation for three days. Manual clearing is not assumed.

scenarios.label: Winter weekend followed by an unoccupied period
scenarios.note: Two occupied days, then five unoccupied days with the battery recovering.

scenarios.label: Full-time winter occupation
scenarios.note: A winter week with mixed weather. Synthetic.

scenarios.label: Partial array failure
scenarios.note: Half the array is unavailable for three days.

scenarios.label: Essential-load-only emergency operation
scenarios.note: Only essential and accessibility loads are served.

Illustrative monthly global horizontal irradiation for eastern Ontario / Canadian Shield conditions, assembled from published regional summaries. Not measured at the site.
Existing Containers Hamlet electrical, ventilation, wood-heat, lighting and water studies.
uncertainties: No surveyed coordinates, measured weather, shading study or solar resource assessment exists for this fictional property.
Panel dimensions, efficiency, temperature coefficients, inverter efficiency and battery usable capacity vary by product.
Tree height, canopy density and winter snow cover are simplified geometric assumptions.
Occupancy and appliance use are assumptions, not metered data.
Battery ageing, cold-weather derating and inverter surge are not fully modeled.
professional_reviews: Licensed electrical contractor and electrical safety authority
Structural engineer for roof and canopy loads
Accessibility consultant for the accessible home
Solar installer for array layout, fixing and maintenance access

internal_gains.note: Occupant and appliance gains are assumptions. Baseline electrical demand is not the same as useful internal gain; only a fraction is counted.

solar.note: Window solar gains use monthly vertical-plane irradiation, a whole-window SHGC and a shading factor for overhangs, deciduous planting and frames. This is not a daylight or overheating model.

wood_heat.note: Wood heat is a design intent. Stove sizing, clearances, make-up air, chimney, storage and WETT review are unresolved.

heat_pump.note: A cold-climate air-source heat pump is assumed. Published performance varies widely; confirm the selected model at the actual outdoor temperatures.

passive.note: A package of plausible passive improvements used to test how much electrical infrastructure can be avoided before adding a heat pump.

thermal.notes: Conceptual thermal model. Envelope areas are derived from the canonical module and opening geometry; U-values, airtightness, gains and solar factors are assumptions, not tested performance.
